title: Implement draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 (i18n localizations, text handling, RFC 3986 URIs, RFC 9457 problem details)
description:
Implement draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 across the crates. The source is /data/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.md at jmap-chat-spec commit 2b85363; it is tracked there as jmap-chat-spec-dhv2. The draft is not yet posted to datatracker (target IETF 127 week) and may change after jmap@ feedback, so re-diff it before each child starts.

What the draft adds:
1. Capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:i18n. The Session value is {}. The account value is {preferredLanguages: String[]|null}.
2. JSCalendar-style `locale` and `localizations` (RFC 8984 4.2.8, 4.6.1) on listed localizable properties, with restrictions:
   - PatchObject keys are localizable properties only.
   - null is allowed only for nullable properties.
   - Keys are unique ignoring case, and no key equals `locale`.
   - An invalid entry is rejected with invalidProperties, not ignored.
   - Stale translations are pruned per untouched language when a base value changes, and `localizations` is echoed in /set `updated`.
3. A `language` argument (language ranges) on /get, /query and /queryChanges:
   - Matching is RFC 4647 Lookup over the localizations keys plus `locale`.
   - "*" is skipped, or selects the default when it is last.
   - Accept-Language MUST NOT change data.
   - queryState reflects the language; a mismatch gives cannotCalculateChanges.
4. Which types are localizable:
   - Mailbox: name
   - Quota: name, description (updates RFC 9425 for opt-in clients)
   - AddressBook: name, description
   - Principal: name, description
   - Calendar: name, description

   Excluded: Identity, ParticipantIdentity and VacationResponse. ContactCard and CalendarEvent keep their own JSContact and JSCalendar localizations.
5. Text handling (updates RFC 8620; SHOULD; no wire change):
   - display-text profile (control characters, U+2028/2029, noncharacters, BOM)
   - no server normalization unless a spec requires it
   - truncation at grapheme cluster boundaries (UAX 29)
   - text filters use the sort collation
   - IANA time zone ids
6. URIs and problem details (updates RFC 8620; SHOULD):
   - URI-valued properties are RFC 3986 URIs; IRIs are mapped per RFC 3987.
   - RFC 7807 becomes RFC 9457.
   - Problem details come from EVERY JMAP HTTP resource: Session, API, upload, download, event source, WS handshake, extension endpoints.
   - title and detail MAY be localized via Accept-Language, with Content-Language set.

Split rule (decision 2026-11-12 on JMAP-y1yu): the crates own wire types, validation, method semantics and error mapping. Storage and transport go through backend hooks. The workspace ships no HTTP, so items about HTTP resources land in jmap-types and jmap-server helpers, jmap-base-client parsing, and the testjig.

Chat adoption (Message `language`, Chat/Space/etc. localizable properties) is NOT in this epic. It waits on jmap-chat-spec-qb21, which changes draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 first.

Children are in dependency order. Child .1 is the design doc and settles the open questions before any code.
notes:
Design: docs/design/updates.md (final 2026-11-15, decisions 27-31). Opt-in is metadata-style (decision 27): JmapBackend::i18n_info hook (default None) + handler helpers; no register_<x>_i18n attach call.
2026-11-15 re-diff: working copy of draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 (uncommitted, after 2b85363) adds BCP 18 / RFC 2277 and W3C string-meta references and a client SHOULD on base direction (first strong character, not the language tag). No server or wire change; mention in client rustdoc under JMAP-cayv.12.
